items.summary: Eli Lilly’s triple-G drug candidate retatrutide has beaten Novo’s Ozempic in a head-to-head phase 3 trial, driving deeper reductions in blood sugar and body weight across the 80-week study.

items.title: GSK predicts ‘some limited impact’ to UK roles as restructuring rolls on
items.summary: GSK’s global restructuring plan is likely to see “some limited impact” to roles on the Big Pharma’s home turf of the U.K., executives have confirmed.

items.title: The 2026 Biotech Graveyard
items.summary: Fierce’s biotech graveyard is an annual tradition in which we remember all the companies we lost over the past year. While we're embracing the spooky spirit of Halloween, we hope the sad stories of drug developers shutting up shop won’t haunt the industry for too long.

items.title: Astellas makes $1.3B bet on Audax’s preclinical push to reverse decades of IL-12 woes
items.summary: Astellas has struck a deal for Audax Biosciences’ IL-12 program, committing up to $285 million in upfront and option fees to secure a chance to license the preclinical immuno-oncology program.

items.title: Artiva lays off 94% of staff after deaths and durability sink autoimmune cell therapy
items.summary: Artiva Biotherapeutics has halted development of an autoimmune disease cell therapy and laid off 94% of its staff after two patients died and durability data fell short of expectations.

items.title: From RAS rivalries to leaked cancer vaccine readouts, ESMO brought the data drama
items.summary: Every ESMO conference is eventful, but the drama kicked into gear earlier than expected this year when the eagerly anticipated phase 3 data for Moderna and Merck & Co.’s cancer vaccine were leaked two days before the Presidential Symposium.

items.title: Parkinson’s-focused Aspen and bispecific biotech Bambusa both shoot for $134M IPOs
items.summary: Parkinson’s disease cell therapy-focused Aspen Neuroscience and bispecific biotech Bambusa Therapeutics are each hoping to raise around $134 million from their respective IPOs.

items.title: Corxel claims oral obesity drug is in the ‘right lane’ as biotech plans SPAC route to Nasdaq
items.summary: Corxel Pharmaceuticals may not have always planned to dust off the SPAC route to the public markets, but the obesity-focused biotech is happy with its choice.

items.title: Labcorp continues acquisition spree as it buys up Millennium Health
items.summary: Labcorp is acquiring Millennium Health to boost the medtech giant’s toxicology testing capabilities throughout the U.S.

items.title: BMS joins 3-year partnership to boost participation in cancer trials
items.summary: The Institute for Healthcare Improvement has partnered with Bristol Myers Squibb on an initiative to expand access to cancer trials.

items.title: Novartis CEO keeps faith in Avidity deal despite taking $1.9B hit from del-desiran fail
items.summary: Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan has insisted that the phase 3 fail for del-desiran is just a “bump” in the Swiss pharma’s wider plans for the drug, despite costing the company an estimated $1.9 billion.

items.title: GSK’s B7-H3 ADC drives 67% cancer risk reduction in Hansoh's phase 3 China trial
items.summary: A phase 3 trial has linked GSK’s risvutatug rezetecan to a 67% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death, providing evidence that B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugates work in relapsed osteosarcoma.

items.title: Boehringer, Microsoft team up to explore digital patient twins for clinical trials
items.summary: Boehringer Ingelheim and Microsoft have launched a collaboration to explore the use of AI-powered digital patient twins to improve clinical trial design.

items.title: Anthropic lays out drug R&D ambitions, risks in mammoth IPO filing
items.summary: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic is pushing deeper into drug discovery, building its own molecular biology lab and investing in research that could eventually produce drug candidates, according to the company's blockbuster IPO filing.

items.title: Lycia leaps onto Nasdaq with upsized $318M IPO as Windward breezes toward listing
items.summary: Lycia Therapeutics went public with an upsized $317.5 million IPO on Friday, while immunology-focused Windward Bio is hoping to catch the same tailwinds.

items.title: ESMO: Why Incyte sees itself ‘neck and neck’ with RevMed in KRAS G12D pancreatic cancer race
items.summary: Incyte has pointed to a spread of phase 1 data for its KRAS G12D inhibitor as evidence that the company has a worthy rival to Revolution Medicines in this increasingly competitive cancer space.

items.title: BioNTech sees ‘limited’ benefit to ADC after phase 3 reveals modest efficacy, ILD cases
items.summary: BioNTech has reported modest efficacy and unexpected safety findings in a phase 3 breast cancer trial, leading the company to conclude its HER2-directed candidate may offer limited benefits in the current treatment landscape.

items.title: BMS sheds light on patient death in CAR-T trial, wants to get program back on track
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has shared more details with Fierce about the death of a patient who received the pharma's investigational CAR-T in a multiple sclerosis trial.

items.title: ESMO: Genmab posts phase 3 win for Elahere rival, ahead of ‘very interesting’ data from Merus buyout
items.summary: Genmab may have arrived in Spain with updated data from a pair of phase 2 studies from the main prize of its Merus buyout, but the company had bigger news to share.

items.title: After GSK's Q3 approval spate, Hibsago preps for 'concentrated' US hep B launch
items.summary: Armed with a trio of recent high-profile approvals, GSK is banking on its specialty medicines to drive its next wave of growth, even as investor enthusiasm cooled Wednesday morning amid reports of restructuring charges and a vaccine sales dip at the British drugmaker.

items.title: Lilly combines global markets under new leadership role as 36-year veteran retires
items.summary: Eli Lilly is consolidating its U.S. and international commercial divisions into a unified department, tapping current U.S. head Ilya Yuffa in a newly created role as president of Lilly Global Markets.

items.title: GSK vows not to ‘park crap on Page 41’ in transparency push
items.summary: GSK CEO Luke Miels has committed to a transparent communication strategy, telling analysts that “we are not going to park crap on Page 41 of a press release and hope none of you notice it.”

items.title: Blue Matter ‘turbocharges’ global reach of comms agency Cognite with acquisition
items.summary: The deal stands to "turbocharge" Cognite's global reach and growth opportunities, chief business officer Sean Cush pointed out.

items.title: Amgen hit with FDA warning letter for ‘misleading’ Vectibix promotion
items.summary: Amgen has been handed an FDA warning letter over a video promoting its cancer drug Vectibix, but the company said that the issues stemmed from an “inadvertent” submission and was not made available publicly.

items.title: Supernus shreds ADHD stigma with Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim
items.summary: The Olympic athlete and Qelbree user is the new face of Supernus' "Ms. Represented" campaign as it looks to reach a younger audience with its ADHD awareness messaging.

items.title: Eversana combines forces with UK-based AI health economics research firm Estima in acquisition
items.summary: Estima's AI and automation capabilities for health economics and outcomes research will help Eversana further leverage the "technology-first solutions" infused into its platform.

items.title: Eli Lilly surges up diabetes reputation rankings to close in on Novo
items.summary: Eli Lilly has jumped up a ranking of the corporate reputations of diabetes drugmakers, putting it hot on the heels of Novo.

items.title: Vanda eyes GLP-1 nausea indication with Nereus phase 3 win in hand
items.summary: Vanda Pharmaceuticals secured a phase 3 win for its motion sickness medicine, Nereus. The drug reduced GLP-1 related vomiting by 27% for patients on Wegovy.

items.title: Teva telegraphs 61 job cuts amid plans to close 'underutilized' New Jersey plant
items.summary: Amid Teva’s return to sales growth, the innovative-generic drugs hybrid has been taking steps to cut costs in parallel, with the downsizing push now reaching a U.S. manufacturing facility in the Garden State.

items.title: UCB’s Bimzelx leads pharma’s Q3 drug ad spend, but who will take the annual prize?
items.summary: We’re heading into the final quarter of the year, and things are heating up in the drug ad spending space.

items.title: Novartis CEO unfazed by high-profile clinical failures, maintains long-term revenue goal
items.summary: Two late-stage clinical failures of high-value projects have not changed Vas Narasimhan’s projection for Novartis over the next 10 years. Based on early launch trajectory in chronic hives and a positive phase 3 readout in relapsing multiple sclerosis, Novartis has increased its peak sales projection for Rhapsido to $8 billion in those indications alone.

items.title: Pfizer heads to FDA with phase 3 myeloma win for Elrexfio
items.summary: Pfizer touted another Elrexfio phase 3 win in earlier-line relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Next up, the drugmaker is taking the data to global regulators in hopes of a label expansion.

items.title: WuXi AppTec bucks DOD uncertainty through Q3, lifting forecast for 2026
items.summary: As it continues to confront a potential existential threat in the United States, CRDMO juggernaut WuXi AppTec’s finances certainly don’t seem to be feeling the pressure.

items.title: Eli Lilly fends off Novo’s legal bid to block GLP-1 marketing claims
items.summary: A U.S. judge has ruled Eli Lilly can keep making marketing claims challenged by Novo pending a ruling on a court case brought by the Danish drugmaker.

items.title: Regeneron lands $270M in renewed US supply pact for approved Ebola med Inmazeb
items.summary: As the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record continues to grip the Democratic Republic of Congo, the United States is taking renewed steps to protect its own citizens from the devastating virus.

items.title: Sun locks in first DTC spot for alopecia areata med Leqselvi
items.summary: The new 60-second spot follows Sun’s fashion-forward “Regrowth Restyled” campaign and aims to spark awareness and hope for people living with alopecia areata.

items.title: Pfizer’s Talzenna combo moves up treatment line with new FDA nod in prostate cancer
items.summary: Pfizer’s Talzenna is now the first PARP inhibitor approved by the FDA to treat men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.

items.title: ESMO: In sac-TMT’s first global phase 3 win, Merck sees ‘pretty consistent’ data with China
items.summary: As a cornerstone of Merck’s post-Keytruda oncology strategy, sac-TMT has cleared a clinical milestone. In its first global phase 3 win, the TROP2 ADC delivered results that are “pretty consistent” with earlier China data, according to Merck’s head of oncology clinical development.

items.title: Novartis' Rhapsido touts solid efficacy with industry-best safety data in RMS phase 3 reveal
items.summary: In new data from Novartis' Remodel-1 and Remodel-2, Rhapsido's safety profile helped compensate for its solid but lower-than-expected efficacy data in RMS.

items.title: Biopharma Companies Must Break the DMTA Linearity
items.summary: Reimagining DMTA as a connected network gives scientists the flexibility to act when needed, with context retained across every decision

items.title: ESMO: Bristol Myers CMO touts ‘5 out of 5’ positive phase 3 trials for bispecific ADC iza-bren
items.summary: Buoyed by a clean sweep of five positive phase 3 readouts in China, Bristol Myers’ Chief Medical Officer Cristian Massacesi, M.D., is voicing growing confidence in the company's first-in-class bispecific ADC iza-bren, even as the New Jersey pharma has yet to match one China study with a global clinical program.

items.title: ESMO: AZ, Hutchmed’s Orpathys combo shows post-Tagrisso power in MET-driven lung cancer
items.summary: AstraZeneca has offered a detailed look at the phase 3 non-small cell lung cancer data that finally position its Hutchmed-partnered Orpathys for an FDA approval more than five years after the MET inhibitor’s initial go-ahead in China.
